title: Grammar in Précis, Paraphrasing and Formal Expression
orientation: Précis writing, paraphrasing, translation and formal answers all require you to change expression while controlling meaning. A fluent rewrite can still be wrong if it turns a possibility into certainty, changes who acted or asserts that a decision was carried out. This lesson gives you an explicit meaning checklist and a complete fictional source passage for reduction work. You will identify essential qualifications, compare near-equivalent sentences and combine claims from different sources without inventing their relationship. The translation activities specify intended meanings so that every learner can participate, whatever their first language. Formal writing tasks then apply the same discipline to correspondence and academic reporting. Length targets are exercise instructions, not universal grammar rules. Open-ended responses have model solutions and concrete rubrics; other defensible versions should be recognised rather than rejected because their wording differs.
outcomes: Reduce an original passage while preserving its essential qualifications.
Combine attributed claims without inventing causation.
Translate meaning notes into idiomatic English.
Draft an explicit formal request with a deadline.

modules.title: Summarising, précis and preserving essential qualifications
modules.definition: A summary selects a text’s central message; a précis is a disciplined concise restatement under specified length and presentation constraints. Neither is a licence to invent facts or strengthen a claim.
foundation: Begin by identifying the source’s topic, main claim, supporting reasons and important limits. A summary is shorter because some detail is omitted, so the claim that every word or every fact must survive is unrealistic. What must survive is the source’s essential meaning at the requested level of detail. If the source says a measure may help some families, a summary saying the measure helps all families is inaccurate. A word target belongs to the assignment. One third is a common exercise convention, not a grammatical law for every summary.
intermediate: Separate a proposition from its examples. If a passage lists several dishes only to illustrate a varied menu, dishes may replace the list. If the passage argues that those particular foods caused an allergy, the exact list may matter. Classification words must not add evaluation: wheat and rice can become crops, but major crops asserts importance not supplied by the list alone. Preserve a condition when it limits the claim: free entry for registered students is not equivalent to free entry. Decide what to omit by its role in the argument, not by length alone.
advanced: Use grammatical compression carefully. The applicants who were selected becomes the selected applicants when the selection meaning and intended scope remain clear. Because the tank leaked can become because of a tank leak. The rewrite may lose tense or explicit participants unless the surrounding text supplies them. A decision to act does not entail action: decided to close the school cannot become closed the school merely to save words. Likewise, not all changes are reversals: failed to confirm is weaker than denied. Compare the original and revision proposition by proposition.
expert: For an original reduction exercise, work from this fictional passage: A village library extended its Saturday opening for a six-week trial. Volunteers staffed the extra hour, so the council did not increase paid staffing. Visitor numbers rose during the trial, mainly among secondary-school pupils. However, the librarian warned that the period overlapped with examinations and was too short to show a lasting change. She recommended a longer trial before any permanent extension. A faithful brief summary reports the increased visits, volunteer arrangement and evidential caution. It must not claim the extension proved a permanent demand or that volunteers could necessarily sustain the arrangement indefinitely.

patterns.form: source claim + essential restriction → shorter equivalent
patterns.meaning: Retains who, what, scope and commitment while reducing wording.

examples.sentence: Selected applicants must attend an interview.
examples.analysis: The reduced relative identifies the selected group.

examples.sentence: The library’s trial coincided with examinations.
examples.analysis: This qualification limits interpretation of increased visits.

examples.sentence: Volunteer staffing accompanied a temporary extension, but a longer trial was recommended.
examples.analysis: The statement preserves the temporary arrangement and recommendation without claiming permanence.

contrasts.a: The committee decided to reopen the hall.
contrasts.note: Both grammatical; the second asserts action that the first alone does not entail.

exceptions: A short summary can omit illustrative detail while retaining essential meaning; a task demanding exact equivalence permits fewer omissions.

mistakes.problem: The trial proves that all pupils need longer hours.
mistakes.repair: The short trial recorded more visits, mainly by secondary pupils; its timing limits conclusions.
mistakes.reason: The original passage supports neither proof nor a universal need.

mistakes.problem: The trial was short, it overlapped with examinations.
mistakes.repair: The trial was short and overlapped with examinations.
mistakes.reason: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a splice in ordinary formal prose.

glossary.definition: A concise restatement meeting a task’s specified constraints.
A condition or limit affecting a claim.

modules.title: Paraphrase, synthesis and faithful reported claims
modules.definition: Paraphrase re-expresses a source’s message; synthesis relates messages from more than one source. Both require grammatical accuracy and faithful treatment of time, modality, attribution and logical relations.
foundation: A paraphrase can alter sentence structure, word choice and information order while preserving the relevant proposition. The team postponed the launch because the battery failed can become Battery failure caused the team to postpone the launch. Both identify the same actor, event and cause. Replacing words with dictionary synonyms without checking their grammatical patterns can produce errors. Depend on does not become depend from because another language uses a different relation word. Keep the source available while checking meaning, then use independent wording rather than copying its sentence and replacing a few words.
intermediate: Track tense and aspect. The plant has closed presents closure with current relevance; the plant closed in March locates a completed event at a specified past time. Either can fit a paraphrase when the necessary time information is retained, but adding March without a source invents a fact. Track modality too: must may express an obligation or a deduction, while may can express permission or possibility. The school may close is not the same as the school must close. Scope matters: not every application succeeded means some failed, not that none succeeded.
advanced: A synthesis must distinguish agreement, difference and silence. Source A says the scheme reduced travel time in two towns; Source B says ticket costs rose. A combined sentence can report both, but cannot claim costs rose because travel time fell unless a source establishes that relationship. Attribution can be compressed without vanishing: According to the survey ... or The authors argue ... identifies whose claim is reported. A reporting verb such as prove, admit or concede may add evidential or evaluative meaning absent from the source. Retain neutral said, report or find when stronger force is unjustified.
expert: Meaning preservation includes entailments and implications. A transformation that makes a restrictive relative supplementary may imply that every member of a group has the property. Removing only or changing the position of a negative can alter scope while leaving the sentence fluent. A paraphrase does not need to reproduce all rhetorical emphasis, but a task may require preserving contrast, caution or a writer’s stance. In expert revision, list the propositions before comparing sentences: actor, action, affected participant, time, quantifier, modality, source and connection. Where two readings remain possible, explain the ambiguity rather than certify a single equivalent mechanically.

patterns.form: Source A reports X, whereas Source B reports Y

patterns.meaning: Denies universality rather than asserting universal failure.

examples.sentence: The report suggests that costs may fall.
examples.analysis: Attribution and possibility both remain visible.
At least one was not renewed; the sentence does not say none were.

examples.sentence: The first survey found shorter journeys; the second recorded higher fares.
examples.analysis: The synthesis relates results without inventing a causal link.

contrasts.note: The first excludes every success; the second permits some successes.

exceptions: A past source can be reported in a present reporting frame when its argument is treated as current; preserve the events’ actual time relations.

mistakes.problem: The report suggests a benefit. → The report proves a benefit.
mistakes.repair: The report indicates a possible benefit.
mistakes.reason: Proves strengthens evidential commitment without support.

mistakes.problem: Only registered readers borrowed the maps. → Registered readers borrowed only the maps.
mistakes.repair: Only registered readers borrowed the maps.
mistakes.reason: Moving only changes its focus from the readers to the objects borrowed.

glossary.definition: A reasoned combination of claims from different sources.
A meaning that must hold if a statement is true in its intended reading.
glossary.example: They left entails that a departure occurred under the ordinary event reading.

modules.title: Translation and formal written answers
modules.definition: Grammatical translation conveys the intended message through the target language’s own constructions. Formal expression selects structures appropriate to a purpose and audience while retaining meaning.
foundation: Translation is not a word-by-word substitution exercise. Languages differ in word order, agreement, articles, pronouns, tense-aspect patterns and conventional combinations. Begin with a plain account of the intended meaning, including who acts and when. Then construct an English sentence from that meaning. A language without English-style articles does not supply an automatic equivalent for a and the; decide whether the English referent is countable and identifiable. Learners can use any first language for this analysis. Urdu-based examples are useful options, not assumptions about every learner’s background.
intermediate: For a controlled translation exercise, the source message can be specified in plain meaning notes instead of requiring knowledge of another language. Message: speaker lives in Multan; residence began in 2019 and continues. Suitable English includes I have lived in Multan since 2019 and I have been living in Multan since 2019. The progressive highlights duration or ongoing activity; the simple perfect is also standard. A literal I am living ... since 2019 is not the ordinary edited pattern for that intended continuing interval. Check meaning and idiom rather than matching one model string.
advanced: Formal correspondence needs clear participants, actions, dates and requested responses. Please send the revised form by Friday is often clearer than a chain of nominalisations. A form such as We request that the form be returned by Friday is also grammatical and may suit a formal institution. The audience determines register; first person, contractions and ordinary short verbs are not universal grammar errors. Regional expressions can be established within their communities while unfamiliar elsewhere. For international readers, choose transparent wording and explain why, instead of treating the regional speaker as grammatically incapable.
expert: Academic answers must distinguish a source’s assertion from the writer’s interpretation. In The author argues that restrictions may reduce demand, the writer reports a cautious claim; changing may to will increases commitment. In translation and paraphrase, preserve negation, quantity, politeness, evidential status and temporal relations even if the new sentence uses a different voice. Back-translation can expose a mismatch, but it is not proof of exact equivalence because several expressions may encode a message. A good rubric recognises alternatives and evaluates specified features. It must not pretend that comparison with a model objectively grades an independently written passage.

patterns.meaning: Uses English grammar to express the intended message.

examples.sentence: Please return the signed declaration by Thursday.
examples.analysis: The action, document and deadline are explicit.

examples.sentence: I have lived in Multan since 2019.
examples.analysis: The present perfect expresses continuing residence from a past starting point.

examples.sentence: The authors argue that the policy may reduce waste.
examples.analysis: The report preserves source and possibility rather than presenting a proven result.

contrasts.note: The second is more transparent for a broad audience; register and regional convention must be distinguished from grammaticality.

exceptions: A regional expression can be standard in its variety; choosing a wider-audience alternative is an editorial decision, not proof of universal error.

mistakes.problem: We request you that send the form.
mistakes.repair: We request that you send the form.
mistakes.reason: The source mixes two complement patterns.

mistakes.problem: The letter says all applicant must signs.
mistakes.repair: The letter says all applicants must sign.
mistakes.reason: All takes plural applicants here; a modal takes the base verb sign.

glossary.definition: Language choices associated with a situation, purpose and audience.
The language into which a message is translated.

questions.prompt: Which statement preserves a decision without asserting that it was carried out?
options: The panel decided to close the room.
The panel had closed the room.
questions.why: Decided to close reports a decision; the other statements assert a closure.

questions.prompt: The source says The treatment may help some patients. Which paraphrase preserves its limits?
options: The treatment could benefit some patients.
questions.why: Could benefit some retains possibility and limited scope.

questions.prompt: Choose the genuine error: The selected candidates must attend interviews.
questions.why: The reduced relative and modal + base form are grammatical.

questions.prompt: Which sentence denies universality without denying every success?
questions.why: Not all permits some successes; no/all failed exclude them.

questions.prompt: For the intended continuing residence since 2017, which form is standard?
questions.why: The present perfect connects past start and continuing residence; continuous perfect is another possible construction outside these options.

questions.prompt: What must a précis length target follow?
options: The number of commas in the source.
questions.why: Length belongs to task requirements; one third is not a universal grammatical law.

questions.prompt: Which synthesis invents causation if sources only report shorter journeys and higher fares?
options: Fares rose because journeys became shorter.
Shorter journeys and higher fares were reported.
One source reports shorter journeys; another reports higher fares.
questions.why: Because asserts a cause that the two isolated findings do not establish.

questions.prompt: Which formal request has a standard complement pattern?
options: We request you that retain a copy.
We request that to retain a copy.
We request that you retain a copy.
questions.why: Request can take a finite that-clause; the other patterns are malformed.

questions.prompt: Which source detail supplies an alternative explanation for the observed attendance rise during the library extension?
options: The extension was held on Saturdays.
questions.why: The examination period could itself influence attendance, so the observed rise cannot simply be attributed to the extension. The other details describe the arrangement but do not supply that stated competing explanation.

questions.prompt: In a meaning-preserving paraphrase, what happens if only moves from readers to maps?
options: Its focus and therefore the claim can change.
questions.why: Only registered readers versus only maps restricts different constituents.

questions.prompt: Classify: a short account of one source’s main claim / a combination of two studies’ differing results.
rubric: Identify the number of source perspectives.
alternatives: Equivalent terminology with explanation is valid.

questions.prompt: Explain why decided to resign cannot simply become resigned in a faithful précis.
questions.model: A decision may not be carried out; resigned asserts actual departure.
alternatives: Equivalent explicit explanations are valid.

questions.prompt: Compress the relative without changing the selected group: Students who were invited may attend.
alternatives: Students invited to the event may attend is valid if the event is identified.

questions.prompt: Complete a cautious report: The authors ____ that the change may help; they do not claim proof.
rubric: Use a verb compatible with caution.
Do not use prove or establish conclusively.
alternatives: Argue or propose may be valid with an appropriate context.

questions.prompt: Preserve the source: Three of ten repairs failed, not all ten. Complete: ____ repairs failed; it is false that ____ failed.
alternatives: Three; every repair is a valid completion.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: Study A found shorter queues. Study B found higher costs. Neither explains why.
questions.model: Study A found shorter queues, while Study B found higher costs; neither identified the causes.
alternatives: Two separate complete sentences are also valid.

questions.prompt: From the library passage, why is permanent demand was proved inaccurate?
questions.model: The trial was short and overlapped with examinations; the librarian recommended more evidence.
rubric: Do not equate increase with proof of permanence.
alternatives: Equivalent evidence-based explanation is valid.

questions.prompt: Order a formal request: by Friday / please / the amended declaration / return.
questions.model: Please return the amended declaration by Friday.
alternatives: By Friday, please return the amended declaration is also valid.

questions.prompt: Explain the scope difference: Only the volunteers checked the forms / The volunteers checked only the forms.
questions.model: First restricts the checkers; second restricts what they checked.
alternatives: Equivalent paraphrases are valid.

questions.prompt: The source lists rice and wheat as examples of crops. Is major crops an exact paraphrase?
questions.model: Not necessarily: major adds importance; crops can summarise the examples if exact members are dispensable.
alternatives: Major is valid only if source context establishes importance.

questions.prompt: Split without losing the concession: Although the trial attracted more visitors, its short duration limited conclusions.
questions.model: The trial attracted more visitors. However, its short duration limited conclusions.
alternatives: Nevertheless can replace however.

questions.prompt: Repair without adding certainty: The findings suggests that all participant may benefit.
questions.model: The findings suggest that all participants may benefit.
rubric: Retain may rather than assert benefit.
alternatives: If only some were intended, that change requires source evidence.

questions.prompt: Meaning notes: no visit yesterday; illness was the reason. Give an English sentence without a literal source-language word order.
questions.model: I did not visit yesterday because I was ill.
alternatives: Because I was ill, I did not visit yesterday is valid.

questions.prompt: Why might The study proves ... be an inaccurate reporting verb when the source says suggests?
questions.model: Proves claims a stronger evidential conclusion than suggests.
alternatives: Demonstrates may also be too strong depending on evidence.

questions.prompt: Edit: The report recommend that each applicant must signs the form. It may prevents delay.
questions.model: The report recommends that each applicant must sign the form. It may prevent delay.
rubric: Use base forms after must and may.
alternatives: The report recommends that each applicant sign the form is a valid mandative alternative.

questions.prompt: Summarise the fictional library passage in 45–65 words.
questions.model: During a six-week Saturday extension at a village library, visits rose, mainly among secondary pupils. Volunteers provided the extra hour without increased paid staffing. Because the short trial overlapped with examinations, the librarian cautioned against assuming a lasting change in demand and recommended a longer test before any permanent extension.
rubric: Preserve staffing arrangement and attendance scope.
Keep recommendation distinct from a decision.
alternatives: Different wording within the assigned range is valid; count using the course convention.

questions.prompt: In The authors argue that costs may fall, identify the reporting frame and modal contribution.
questions.model: The authors argue attributes the claim; may marks possible reduction rather than certainty.
alternatives: Equivalent functional description is valid.

questions.prompt: Draft two sentences asking an office to correct your fictional record and reply by a date.
questions.model: Please correct the spelling of my surname in the attached record. I would appreciate confirmation by 12 November.
alternatives: Other polite clear requests are valid; no rare vocabulary is required.

corrections.prompt: Repair: The summary contain three main point.
corrections.model: The summary contains three main points.
alternatives: Three main points appear in the summary is valid.

corrections.prompt: No change if grammatical: The writer suggests that the scheme may reduce waste in some schools.
rubric: Accept layered attribution, possibility and scope.
Do not delete a meaningful qualification.
alternatives: The scheme might reduce waste in some schools, the writer suggests is valid.

corrections.prompt: Correct: We request that the form is returned by Friday. Express a request using mandative be.
corrections.model: We request that the form be returned by Friday.
alternatives: Should be returned is a standard British alternative.

corrections.prompt: Repair a summary that wrongly turns decided to appeal into appealed. Original: The applicant decided to appeal but had not filed papers.
corrections.model: The applicant decided to appeal but had not yet filed papers.
rubric: Do not assert an appeal occurred.
alternatives: A paraphrase explicitly retaining the decision and non-filing is valid.

corrections.prompt: Correct: According to report, the results was uncertain. The intended report has already been identified.
corrections.model: According to the report, the results were uncertain.
rubric: Use definite the for the identified report.
alternatives: The identified report described the results as uncertain is valid.

corrections.prompt: No change if grammatical: I have been living here since 2020.
rubric: Do not replace since with for before a starting year.
alternatives: I have lived here since 2020 is also valid.

corrections.prompt: Repair scope to mean some applications failed, without saying none succeeded: No applications succeeded.
alternatives: Some applications failed is valid.

corrections.prompt: Repair: She asked me that submit the revised statement.
corrections.model: She asked me to submit the revised statement.
alternatives: She asked that I submit ... is valid.

transformations.prompt: Paraphrase without changing cause or actor: Because the supplier delivered late, the team postponed installation.
transformations.model: Late delivery by the supplier caused the team to postpone installation.
rubric: Retain the causal relation and postponement.
alternatives: The team postponed installation because of the supplier’s late delivery is valid.

transformations.prompt: Convert to a formal request retaining deadline: Please send us the signed copy before Monday.
transformations.model: We request that you send us the signed copy before Monday.
rubric: Retain before Monday, not by an ambiguous later date.
alternatives: We ask you to send us ... is valid.

writing.prompt: Write two outputs from the fictional library passage: (1) a 60–80-word précis; (2) a three-sentence formal note asking the council to approve a longer trial, clearly distinguishing evidence from recommendation.
writing.model:
(1) During a village library’s six-week Saturday extension, visits rose, mainly among secondary pupils. Volunteers provided the extra hour without an increase in paid staffing. The librarian cautioned that the short trial overlapped with examinations, so it did not establish a lasting change in demand or prove that longer hours caused the rise. A longer test was recommended before any permanent extension.

(2) Please consider approving a longer trial of the Saturday extension. Visits rose during the initial trial, but its short duration and overlap with examinations limit what can be inferred. A further trial would provide more evidence before the council decides whether to make the change permanent.
rubric: Précis: retain source scope, arrangement and caution; follow assigned length.
Formal note: make the request explicit without claiming proven permanent demand.
Self-review using the rubric; a model is not automated grading.
alternatives: Alternative original outputs are valid when they preserve the stated features.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 21: Why can may become might after a past reporting verb?
recall.model: It can adopt an earlier viewpoint while retaining possibility.
alternatives: May can remain for current relevance.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 20: In the officer appointed in June, what has been reduced?
recall.model: A relative such as the officer who was appointed in June.
rubric: Do not invent the appointing agent.
alternatives: A reduced relative/non-finite modifier label is valid.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 26: When can a nominalisation help cohesion?
recall.model: When an earlier event becomes a topic, as reject the bid → this rejection.
rubric: Explain continuity rather than automatic formality.
alternatives: Other accurate event-noun examples are valid.

checklist: I can list the source’s central propositions.
I preserve modality, quantity and attribution.
I do not turn decisions into completed actions.
I check the requested length convention.
